endorsements.quote: CHART includes 12 items and 39 subitems to promote transparent and comprehensive reporting of chatbot health advice studies.

unlisted_practices: Clinical journals should adopt the CHART reporting guideline for chatbot health advice studies.
Authors of chatbot health advice studies should report the model name, version, and open- or closed-source status, prompts, query dates and locations, and all chatbot responses.
Authors of chatbot health advice studies should report whether ethics approval was obtained, particularly when patients are included.
Funders should invest in high-quality benchmarking and validation studies of generative AI chatbots in the healthcare setting of interest.
Regulators should ensure generative AI developers put data security measures in place according to risk category.
Researchers should evaluate and report chatbot responses for potentially harmful, biased, or misleading content.
Authors should state whether permission or licensing was obtained for copyrighted data used in training or evaluation.
Authors should share code, training data, and model parameters to support transparency and mitigate uncertainty about data provenance.

screen.reason: This paper presents the CHART reporting guideline/checklist developed via Delphi consensus for reporting studies of chatbot health advice.
